copy.en:
What makes up a mixture?

A mixture is simply made when two or more different substances are mixed all together!
copy.tl:
Ano ang bumubuo ng isang mixture?

Ang isang mixture ay binubuo ng dalawa o higit pang mga sangkap na pinagsama-sama nang magkaiba!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghimo sa usa ka mixture?

Ang usa ka mixture gilangkuban sa duha o sobra pa ka lain-laing sangkap nga gisagol-sagol!

copy.tl: Eksaktong sa gitna ng scale ay apatite! Ang mineral na ito ay may Mohs hardness na 5.
copy.bis: Sakto sa tunga sa scale mao ang apatite! Kini nga mineral adunay Mohs hardness nga 5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use the Mohs hardness scale! It rates hardness from 1 (softest talc) to 10 (hardest diamond) by seeing which can scratch the other.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size

copy.en:
How do scientists measure if a mineral is soft or hard?

They use the Mohs hardness scale! It rates hardness from 1 (softest talc) to 10 (hardest diamond) by seeing which can scratch the other.
copy.tl:
Paano sinusukat ng mga siyentipiko kung malambot o matigas ang mineral?

Ginagamit nila ang Mohs hardness scale! Sinusukat nito ang tigas mula 1 (pinakamalambot na talc) hanggang 10 (pinakamatigas na diamond) base sa kung sino ang makakagasgas.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsukod sa mga siyentipiko kung humok o gahi ang mineral?

Nagagamit nila ang Mohs hardness scale! Nagsukod kini sa kagahi gikan sa 1 (pinakahumok nga talc) ngadto sa 10 (pinakagahi nga diamond) base kung kinsa ang makagasgas sa lain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It measures mineral hardness from 1, the softest, all the way to 10, the hardest.

copy.en:
How do we measure how hard a mineral is?

We use the Mohs scale! It measures mineral hardness from 1, the softest, all the way to 10, the hardest.
copy.tl:
Paano natin sinusukat ang tigas ng isang mineral?

Ginagamit natin ang Mohs scale! Sinusukat nito ang tigas ng mineral mula 1, ang pinakamalambot, hanggang 10, ang pinakamatigas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsukod sa gahi sa usa ka mineral?

Gamiton nato ang Mohs scale! Nagsukod kini sa gahi sa mineral gikan sa 1, ang pinakahumok, ngadto sa 10, ang pinakagahi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because they're covered in enamel — the hardest material in your whole body!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions tooth enamel and molars grinding food. It does not describe how any human body system works, including the digestive system, so it does not directly support G4-L-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because they're covered in enamel — the hardest material in your whole body!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on mechanical processing of food by molars, but it lacks the required labeled diagram tracing food through the digestive tract and does not explain digestive processes. It is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en:
Why don't molars wear out from grinding food?

Because they're covered in enamel — the hardest material in your whole body! That tough coating lets them crush hard food every day.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi agad nasisira ang bagang?

Dahil nababalot ito ng enamel — ang pinakamatigas na bahagi ng ating katawan! Kaya nitong durugin ang matitigas na pagkain araw-araw nang hindi agad nasisira.
copy.bis:
Ngano dili dali madaot ang bag-ang?

Kay gibalotan kini og enamel — ang pinakagahi nga bahin sa atong lawas! Mao nga makahimo kini og pagdugmok sa gahi nga pagkaon adlaw-adlaw nga dili dali madaot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: resists both termites and rotting
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that molave wood resists termites and rotting, which touches on resistance to decay (biodegradability), but it does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. It only gives a single factual claim without explaining the chemical nature, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why does molave wood last so long?

Molave wood lasts for a very long time because it resists both termites and rotting!
copy.tl:
Bakit matibay ang kahoy na molave?

Matagal bago masira ang kahoy na molave dahil hindi ito madaling kainin ng anay o mabulok!
copy.bis:
Nganong lig-on ang kahoy nga molave?

Dugay madaot ang kahoy nga molave kay dili kini dali kan-on sa anay o madunot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mollusks are soft-bodied animals, and many of them grow a hard shell to protect themselves

assignedReviews.reason: A soft body and protective shell is invertebrate-adjacent, but the card does not contrast backbone versus no backbone.

copy.en: Mollusks are soft-bodied animals, and many of them grow a hard shell to protect themselves.
copy.tl: Ang mga molusko ay mga hayop na may malambot na katawan, at marami sa kanila ay may matigas na kabibe na pananggalang.
copy.bis: Ang mga molusko mga hayop nga humok ug lawas, ug daghan kanila adunay gahi nga kabhang nga pangpanalipod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The negative sign simply shows direction, not that it's less than zero.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that momentum depends on the mass and the velocity of a moving object that can be used to predict the impact the object will have if it hits another object
assignedReviews.reason: The card only clarifies that a negative momentum value indicates direction. It does not explain that momentum depends on mass and velocity, nor does it address using momentum to predict impact. This is a peripheral clarification about momentum, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en:
Can momentum be negative?

Yes! But it just means the object is moving in the opposite direction. The negative sign simply shows direction, not that it's less than zero.
copy.tl:
Pwede bang maging negative ang momentum?

Oo! Pero nangangahulugan lang ito na gumagalaw ang bagay sa kabaligtarang direksyon. Ang negative sign ay nagpapakita lang ng direksyon, hindi na mas maliit ito sa zero.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang negatibo ang momentum?

Oo! Apan nagpasabot lang kini nga naglihok ang butang sa kontra nga direksyon. Ang negatibo nga timaan nagpakita lang sa direksyon, dili nga ubos pa kini sa zero.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because several kinds are endemic — found only here and nowhere else on Earth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that Philippine monitor lizards are endemic, but it does not classify them as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable. Endemism is not the same as threat status, so the card does not directly support the competency's classification action.

copy.en:
Why are the Philippines' monitor lizards special?

Because several kinds are endemic — found only here and nowhere else on Earth! That's one reason our islands are so important for studying animals.
copy.tl:
Bakit espesyal ang mga bayawak sa Pilipinas?

Dahil maraming uri ang endemic — matatagpuan lamang dito at wala saanman pa sa mundo! Ito ang dahilan kung bakit napakahalaga ng ating kapuluan sa pag-aaral ng iba't ibang hayop.
copy.bis:
Nganong espesyal ang mga bayawak sa Pilipinas?

Tungod kay daghang matang ang endemic — makita lamang dinhi ug wala nay laing dapit sa kalibutan! Mao kini usa ka rason nga importante kaayo ang atong kapuropuroan sa pagtuon sa lainlaing mananap.

copy.en: Many monkeys live together in groups so they can help each other and watch out for danger.
copy.tl: Maraming unggoy ang namumuhay nang sama-sama sa grupo para magtulungan at magbantayan sa panganib.
copy.bis: Daghang unggoy nagpuyo nga magkauban sa grupo aron magtinabangay ug magbantay sa peligro.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions two seasonal winds but does not involve observing, recording, or describing weather changes, types, or patterns as required by G3-E-4. copy.en:
Where do the words 'habagat' and 'amihan' come from?

They are local names! Filipinos have used them for a long time to describe our two big seasonal winds.
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang mga salitang 'habagat' at 'amihan'?

Katutubong pangalan sila! Matagal nang ginagamit ng mga Pilipino para sa dalawang malaking hangin pana-panahon.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang mga pulong nga 'habagat' ug 'amihan'?

Lumad nga mga ngalan sila! Dugay na nga gigamit sa mga Pilipino alang sa duha ka dagkong hangin matag-panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Moon rock samples show they share similar oxygen isotope ratios, supporting the giant impact hypothesis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Moon rock samples show they share similar oxygen isotope ratios, supporting the giant impact hypothesis.

copy.en:
Are the Moon and Earth made of the same stuff?

Yes! Moon rock samples show they share similar oxygen isotope ratios, supporting the giant impact hypothesis. But the Moon has a much smaller iron core, meaning the impactor added mostly silicate rock!
copy.tl:
Gawa ba sa parehong materyales ang Moon at Earth?

Oo! Ang mga Moon rock sample ay nagpapakita na may magkatulad na oxygen isotope ratios, sumusuporta sa giant impact hypothesis. Pero mas maliit ang iron core ng Moon, ibig sabihin nagdagdag ang impactor ng silicate rock!
copy.bis:
Gihimo ba sa samang materyales ang Moon ug Yuta?

Oo! Ang mga Moon rock sample nagpakita nga adunay susama nga oxygen isotope ratios, nagsuporta sa giant impact hypothesis. Apan mas gamay ang iron core sa Moon, pasabot nagdugang ang impactor og silicate rock!

copy.en:
Why does the Moon sometimes look like a thin curved sliver?

That's a crescent moon! We see it when only a small part of the Moon facing us is lit up by the Sun.
copy.tl:
Bakit minsan hugis-kurba at manipis ang itsura ng Buwan?

Iyan ang crescent moon! Nakikita natin ito kapag maliit na bahagi lang ng Buwan sa harap natin ang natatamaan ng sikat ng Araw.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang Bulan usahay murag nipis ug kurba nga tipik?

Mao na ang crescent moon! Makita nato kini kon gamay ra nga bahin sa Bulan nga nag-atubang kanato ang nasilawan sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It takes about one month, or around 29 days, for the Moon to complete its full cycle of phases!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Moon's cycle but does not address how or when the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky. It provides no support for the guided exploration and recording of celestial motion.

copy.en: It takes about one month, or around 29 days, for the Moon to complete its full cycle of phases!
copy.tl: Tumatagal ng halos isang buwan, o mga 29 na araw, para makumpleto ng Buwan ang buong siklo ng mga yugto nito!
copy.bis: Mga usa ka bulan, o gibana-bana 29 ka adlaw, ang gikinahanglan aron makompleto sa Bulan ang tibuok siklo sa mga yugto niini!

copy.en: Europa, a moon of Jupiter, is believed to have a vast ocean of water beneath its thick crust of ice!
copy.tl: Ang Europa, isang buwan ng Jupiter, ay pinaniniwalaang may malawak na karagatan ng tubig sa ilalim ng makapal na yelo nito!
copy.bis: Ang Europa, usa ka bulan sa Jupiter, gituohan nga adunay halapad nga dagat sa tubig ilalom sa baga niini nga yelo!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions the Moon and the absence of wind/rain, which is a specific fact about the Moon's environment. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition as required by G5-E-11.

copy.en: Astronaut footprints on the Moon stay for a very long time! There is no wind or rain to wipe them away.
copy.tl: Napakatagal nananatili ang mga bakas ng paa ng astronaut sa Buwan! Walang hangin o ulan doon na magbubura sa mga ito.
copy.bis: Magpabilin og dugay kaayo ang mga tunob sa astronaut sa Bulan! Walay hangin o ulan didto nga mopapas niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Moon's surface gravity is about 1.6 m/s², which is much weaker than Earth's 9.8 m/s²!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a numerical comparison of the Moon's gravity to Earth's, but does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or describe its predictable effects on objects on Earth. It shares the topic of gravity but does not directly support the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Moon's surface gravity is about 1.6 m/s², which is much weaker than Earth's 9.8 m/s²!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Moon as a celestial object but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their main features and composition. The Moon's gravity is a minor detail, not substantive support for the competency.

copy.en:
How strong is gravity on the Moon compared to Earth?

The Moon's surface gravity is about 1.6 m/s², which is much weaker than Earth's 9.8 m/s²!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalakas ang grabidad sa Buwan kumpara sa Daigdig?

Ang grabidad sa ibabaw ng Buwan ay halos 1.6 m/s², mas mahina kaysa sa 9.8 m/s² ng Daigdig!
copy.bis:
Pila ka kusog ang grabidad sa Bulan kumpara sa Yuta?

Ang grabidad sa ibabaw sa Bulan mga 1.6 m/s², mas huyang kaysa sa 9.8 m/s² sa Yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The moon jellyfish is one of the most common jellyfish in Philippine bays

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine animal but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify it by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). It only identifies the jellyfish as common in Philippine waters, with no habitat classification or required format.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (four circle shapes) of a jellyfish, but does not identify the role of that part in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en: The moon jellyfish is one of the most common jellyfish in Philippine bays — you can recognize it by the four circle shapes visible in the middle of its clear body.
copy.tl: Ang moon jellyfish ay isa sa pinakakaraniwang jellyfish sa mga look ng Pilipinas — makikilala ito sa apat na bilog na hugis na makikita sa gitna ng transparent na katawan nito.
copy.bis: Ang moon jellyfish usa sa pinaka-komon nga jellyfish sa mga look sa Pilipinas — mailhan kini pinaagi sa upat ka bilog nga hulma nga makita sa sentro sa transparent nga lawas niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We see only one face of the Moon because it spins on its axis in the same time it takes to orbit Earth, called tidal locking!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate seasons, star patterns, and eclipses. copy.en:
Why do we only see one face of the Moon?

We see only one face of the Moon because it spins on its axis in the same time it takes to orbit Earth, called tidal locking!
copy.tl:
Bakit iisang mukha lang ng Buwan ang nakikita natin?

Nakikita natin ang iisang mukha ng Buwan dahil magkasing-tagal ang pag-ikot nito sa sarili at sa Earth, na tinatawag na tidal locking!
copy.bis:
Nganong usa ra ka nawong sa Bulan ang atong makita?

Usa ra ka nawong sa Bulan ang atong makita kay parehas ra ang gidugayon sa pagtuyok niini sa kaugalingon ug sa paglibot sa Earth, nga gitawag og tidal locking!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Moon orbits Earth at about 1 kilometer per second!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the Moon's orbital speed. It does not involve drawings or a model, does not show motion relative to the Sun, and does not explain moon phases.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Moon orbits Earth at about 1 kilometer per second!

assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a speed value but does not teach that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It uses the concept without defining or explaining it.

copy.en:
How fast does the Moon orbit Earth?

The Moon orbits Earth at about 1 kilometer per second!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis umiikot ang Buwan sa Mundo?

Ang Buwan ay umiikot sa Mundo sa bilis na humigit-kumulang 1 kilometro kada segundo!
copy.bis:
Unsa katulin ang Buwan sa paglibot sa Kalibotan?

Ang Bulan moliyok sa Kalibotan sa tulin nga mga 1 ka kilometro kada segundo!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
